questions.question: At an integer starting age, a mortality model assumes uniform distribution of deaths (UDD) in each year of age. Which interpretation follows?
options: The complete future lifetime must be uniform over all remaining ages.
All annual death probabilities must equal one another.
Every life dies exactly halfway through its death year.
Within-year death fractions are uniform; annual mortality may vary.

questions.question: At integer age $x$, annual death probability is $0<q<1$ and the starting cohort has size $l_x>0$. A model sets $l_{x+s}=l_x(1-qs^2)$ for $0\le s\le1$. Both annual endpoints are correct. Which assessment follows?
options: It violates UDD because deaths are not linear in elapsed time.
It satisfies UDD because correct annual endpoints determine interpolation.
It satisfies UDD because the same annual input $q$ is used throughout.
It violates UDD because survivor counts must decrease exponentially.

questions.question: At integer issue age $x$, continuous future lifetime $T_x$ is finite with probability one. Define $K_x=\lfloor T_x\rfloor$ and $R_x=T_x-K_x$. UDD is imposed in every subsequent year. What conditional law is required for every $k$ with $P(K_x=k)>0$?
options: $R_x\mid K_x=k$ is uniform on $(0,k+1)$.
$R_x\mid K_x=k$ equals $1/2$ with probability one.
$R_x\mid K_x=k$ is uniform on $(0,1)$, unchanged by $k$.
$R_x\mid K_x=k$ must have a different law for each $k$.

questions.question: Under UDD at integer age $x$, annual death probability is $q_x\in(0,1)$ and survivor proportion at elapsed fraction $s$ is $1-sq_x$. Mortality force is $\mu_{x+s}=q_x/(1-sq_x)$ for $0\leq s<1$. Why can the force increase despite uniform death density within that year?
options: Uniform deaths require the force itself to remain constant.
The same death density is divided by a decreasing survivor proportion.
The original-cohort death density increases as the year progresses.
The annual death probability $q_x$ is replaced by a larger input at each fractional age.

questions.question: Under UDD in the year starting at integer age $x$, annual death probability is $q_x=0$. The cohort starts with $l_x>0$ survivors. What happens to survivor counts and mortality force within that year?
options: Survivor count decreases linearly and mortality force increases.
Survivor count stays $l_x$ but force is one because survival is certain.
Survivor count reaches zero at year end, while force remains zero.
Survivor count stays $l_x$ and mortality force is zero.

questions.question: At an integer starting age, annual death probability is 0.2 and UDD holds within that year. What is probability of death within the first quarter-year, measured from that starting age?
UDD holds between integer ages 60 and 61, with annual death probability 0.1 from age 60. What is the conditional probability of dying between ages 60.5 and 60.75, given survival to age 60.5?
Within a UDD year, annual death probability from integer age $x$ is $q_x=0.2$. What is mortality force at age $x+0.5$?
For integer issue age, define $K=\lfloor T\rfloor$ and $R=T-K$ from continuous future lifetime $T$. UDD holds in every future year, and $P(K=2)=0.3$. What is $P(K=2,\ R>0.8)$?

Under UDD from integer age $x$, annual death probability is $q_x\in[0,1]$. For fractions $0\leq s\leq s+t\leq1$, conditional survival over the next $t$ years from age $x+s$ is proposed as $[1-(s+t)q_x]/[1-sq_x]$. What is the necessary and sufficient survivor condition for this ratio conditioning to be defined?
options: $1-sq_x\geq0$

questions.question: A continuous lifetime is constructed as $T=K+R$, where $P(K=0)=P(K=1)=1/2$. Conditional on $K=0$, $R$ is uniform on $(0,1/2)$; conditional on $K=1$, $R$ is uniform on $(1/2,1)$. The marginal $R$ is uniform on $(0,1)$. What does this imply about the claim that marginal uniformity alone establishes all-year UDD?
options: The claim holds because a uniform R necessarily has the same conditional law in each year.
The claim fails: R is marginally uniform but its law depends on K.
The claim fails because K must itself be uniform over every possible nonnegative integer.
The claim holds because the equal probabilities of the two years imply independence.

questions.question: UDD holds separately in each year of age. Annual death probabilities are $q_x=0.1$ from integer age $x$ and $q_{x+1}=0.2$ from age $x+1$. What is survival from age $x+0.5$ to age $x+1.5$, conditional on reaching $x+0.5$?
UDD holds within an integer-age year. Among survivors at its midpoint, probability of dying before the year ends is 0.1. What annual death probability from the integer-age origin is implied?

At integer issue age, future lifetime is $T=K+R$, with $K=\lfloor T\rfloor$. Under all-year UDD, $R$ is uniform on $(0,1)$ and independent of $K$. Suppose $P(K=0)=0.2$, $P(K=1)=0.3$ and $P(K=2)=0.5$. What is $P(T>1.6)$?

A lifetime $T$ is a mixture: with probability one half it is uniform on $(0,1)$, and with probability one half it is uniform on $(1.5,2)$. Define $K=\lfloor T\rfloor$ and $R=T-K$. An analyst applies the all-year UDD conclusion from the fact that deaths in the first year are uniform. Which diagnosis is correct?
options: First-year UDD fails because the unconditional density there is only one half.
All-year UDD holds because each component has a uniform density on its own interval.
R is uniform but K and R are dependent, so only independence fails.
First-year UDD holds, but R is not uniform over (0,1) across this lifetime law.

questions.question: At integer age $x$, future lifetime $T$ is uniform on $(0,1)$, so the year satisfies UDD with annual death probability one. A survivor at age $x+0.5$ has residual lifetime $U=T-0.5$ conditional on $T>0.5$. Define its new fractional part $R^\ast=U-\lfloor U\rfloor$. Does the integer-origin uniform-fraction conclusion make $R^\ast$ uniform on $(0,1)$?
options: No: R* is uniform on (0,0.5), because the origin has moved inside the year.
Yes: the UDD fractional-part conclusion holds unchanged after any age shift.
No: R* must equal 0.5 because every survivor has half a year left.
Yes: conditioning on survival preserves the original complete lifetime support (0,1).

questions.question: UDD holds separately in two years starting at integer age $x$, with unknown annual death probabilities $q_0,q_1$. Survival from $x$ to $x+1.5$ is $17/25$. Conditional survival from $x+0.5$ to $x+2$ is $28/45$. Which pair $(q_0,q_1)$ fits both quotes?
Under all-year UDD from integer issue age, $T=K+R$, with $P(K=0)=0.2$, $P(K=1)=0.8$, and $R$ uniform on $(0,1)$ independently of $K$. What is $P(R>0.5\mid T<1.5)$?
